title: Choose A New Artwork To Make
objective: Test simple prints and choose a new print-and-collage artwork; preserve the pupil’s starting idea and material trials as process evidence.

blocks.text: Explore · Part C · Create. Choose a new artwork to make.
Today you will try a print tool, choose an idea, and keep a record of your first steps. Your choices will guide a new work over four lessons.
We are making a new print and collage. A print is a mark pressed from one surface to another. A collage joins pieces to make one image.
Keep your test marks and first layout. Part C needs both the steps you took and the final artwork. Today begins that trail; the final piece comes later.
You can point, speak, type or write to show your choices. You may make a pattern or a made-up place. Your art does not have to tell a story about your life.

This deck supports Explore Part C, Create. Part C requires an artwork, a record of the PROCESS, and the final work. The new print-and-collage activity is distinct from the drawing and paper sculpture in Part A and the live or active exploration in Part B. Do not relabel a finished A or B work as C. Source: tools/artsaward/SPEC.json, Explore and universal rules. Mark each part P / A / N. Overall Pass allows ONE Attempted. Any Not Attempted = Below Pass. Results are Pass or Below Pass only. The whole Explore digital portfolio has a 10-file cap. Organise it by part; four cumulative files, Explore-A, Explore-B, Explore-C and Explore-D, are a suggested arrangement, not one new file per lesson. Every evidence locator must name the actual file plus page, slide or timecode. The three assessment areas are art form knowledge and understanding, creativity, and communication. Core, Extend and Challenge vary support within Explore; each retains the pupil’s own artwork, process record and final work across C1–C4. Only an adviser trained at Explore may assess. Delivery is through a validated centre; staff must confirm these conditions, which this deck does not assert are met. Adults may scribe the pupil’s exact words and check them back. They must not write plans, reviews or evidence for the pupil. Staff may record factual observations of access support separately. No visit, booking, meeting or date is asserted. Keep the theme on art choices; no private life account is required.

Explore Part C C1 begins a distinct creation activity. Prepare fresh backing card, scrap paper, washable paint in shallow trays, blunt sponge shapes or corrugated card print tools, glue sticks and accessible scissors. Check tools, allergies and local handling rules. Offer pre-cut pieces and easy-grip tools. Use dry prepared texture paper as an access choice if wet paint is unsuitable; the pupil still tests, selects, arranges and makes their own new collage. Prepare a drying area and a means to preserve samples or images. Photograph artwork only if appropriate; record who took each image. Model on fresh adult scraps. The process and final artwork will accumulate through C1–C4.

stages.title: Arrival · retrieve

blocks.text: Think about how you used a tool in Part A. You may look at your own drawing or paper form to help you recall a skill. Which action helped you control a line, fold or join?
Carry a skill into this task, but start with fresh materials. Your new image can use a repeated shape, a bold edge, or a quiet space. It will be a new work with its own steps.
Put a clean backing card in front of you. Look at the print tools. Point to a tool you want to test and say what sort of mark you think it may leave.

stages.data-ta1: Offer earlier work for recall only. Keep finished A and B work separate from the new C activity. Accept a pointed choice without requiring a public explanation.

stages.title: Starter · create the need

blocks.text: Look at a strip with one print and a strip with the same print repeated. A repeat can lead your eye across a page. A single mark can draw your eye to one spot.
A print may look different from its tool. Paint can fill a small gap. A light press may miss an edge. We need to try the tool before we choose how to use it.
Which would help you choose: a guess about the tool, or a test on scrap paper? Explain by pointing to the mark you would inspect.
Our task is to make an image from prints and paper pieces. You can choose a pattern, a path through shapes, or a made-up skyline. These are starting points, not answers to copy.

stages.data-ta1: Make the two quick sample strips in front of pupils using the same blunt tool. Describe marks aloud as needed; no unseen worksheet is required.

stages.title: I Do · model

blocks.text: Watch the test before you try your own. I put a thin layer of paint on the flat face of a sponge. I press it straight down on scrap paper, hold it still, then lift it straight up.
I can see a shape with a clear edge. I try again with more paint. This mark has a thick blob at one side. For my idea, the thin coat gives the edge I want.
I let the print dry. Then I tear a dry paper strip, place it beside the print, and move it across the edge. Part of the print is now hidden. That is overlap.
I want my marks to look like stepping stones. I leave gaps to make a path. I do not glue yet. I keep both tests and make a quick sketch of the loose layout.

blocks.title: Try before you choose
blocks.caption: A small test gives you a real mark to choose from.
blocks.alt: COAT: use a thin layer. PRESS: hold the tool still. LIFT: move straight up. LOOK: check the edge. A small test gives you a real mark to choose from.

blocks.text: This is my model, not your plan. You may want a soft edge or a dense patch. A different choice can work if it gives the effect you want.

stages.data-ta1: Demonstrate each action with real materials before pupil making. State that the adult example shows a method only. Preserve both model tests rather than repainting over the first.

stages.title: We Do · everyone commits

blocks.text: Sort these cards into TEST, CHOICE, or FINAL WORK. Use the numbers on the screen. You can point, say the group, or write a letter beside each number.

items: 1. Two scrap prints show a light press and a firm press.
2. I will use wide gaps to make my path feel open.
3. The new collage is finished and all its pieces are fixed.
4. I tried rough paper and smooth paper with the same tool.

blocks.text: Check the key: TEST has 1 and 4. CHOICE has 2. FINAL WORK has 3. A test shows what happened. A choice says what you decide to do.
Do we have card 3 yet? No. We can keep a start today without claiming the work is finished. We will save the final piece when it is ready.

stages.data-ta1: Every card and the key are visible. Cover or delay the key until everyone responds. Use the responses to check the difference between tests, intentions and finished work.

stages.title: I Do 2 · connect

blocks.text: I can learn from an old skill without turning an old work into my new piece. I used firm pressure for a fold in Part A. Here I use steady pressure to make a print.

blocks.title: A skill can lead to fresh work
blocks.caption: Keep the new work and its own making steps.
blocks.alt: EARLIER SKILL: steady hands on a fold, learned in Part A. NEW ARTWORK: fresh prints and pieces, own layout for Part C. Keep the new work and its own making steps.

blocks.text: I choose a small card so I can reach the whole surface. I choose a sponge that is easy to hold. These choices help me make the work myself.
On a blank page I put a rough sketch, a test print and my own words: I want a path with wide gaps. A sketch need not be neat. It needs to help me remember the start.
If I speak my idea, an adult can write my exact words and read them back. The adult does not choose the image or write a plan for me.

stages.data-ta1: Model an accessible tool choice and a genuine start record. Use a plain page or the printed focus rows; do not imply another planning sheet exists.

stages.title: We Do 2 · lab

blocks.text: On scrap paper, try a small print with a thin coat. Lift the tool without sliding it. Try another mark beside it. Keep both so you can look from one to the other.
Let the tests dry in the agreed place. While they dry, place dry paper pieces on your fresh backing. Try a gap, then an overlap. Which helps your idea?
Tell a partner or adult which test you want to use. Point to the part of the mark that helped you decide. You may choose a different tool and try again.

stages.data-ta1: Support the grip or steady the paper as needed while retaining the pupil’s creative choices. For the dry route, compare textured paper trials before arranging pieces.

stages.title: Independent · evidence

blocks.text: Choose your new image and start a loose layout. Use your tests to choose shapes, marks and spaces. You can work with a few large pieces or several small ones.
Keep a sketch or image of the layout before you move it. Add a test sample and a short note or recording of your idea. Say which tool or paper you chose.

items: Core: use large ready-cut pieces, a chosen print tool and spoken words or pointing. Make your own layout. Keep the tests and start record, then keep the final artwork when it is made.
Extend: make and label your own tests, choose a layout and record your reason. Keep the process trail and the final artwork as the work grows.
Challenge: test two ways to space the same marks. Choose one for a reason. Keep both trials, your process trail and the final artwork.

blocks.text: Your route changes the help you use. It does not remove the making or its record. Check that your words say what you chose, not what someone else wanted.

stages.data-ta1: All routes retain the same Part C evidence requirement across the sequence. Scribe verbatim only, read it back, and preserve the pupil’s own choice. Do not glue a pupil’s layout without their decision.

stages.title: Exit · check the trail

blocks.text: Put your name or agreed code on the back of your work. Store wet prints flat. Keep dry trials where they can be found next time.
Add today’s start to your Explore-C file. Write the actual file name and page or slide. For a sound or video record, give the file name and timecode. Name who took any photo.
Check that you have a new idea and real tests. Point to what you plan to do next. Today shows the start of making; your Part C trail will also need the finished work.

stages.data-ta1: Check the actual saved location. If digitising later, keep the labelled physical record and record the pending action; do not invent a file locator.

print.intro: Try prints and paper pieces for a new artwork. Keep your real tests and first idea. Add the final work when it is made.
focusRows: My new image idea and the tools or paper I choose
A test I made and what its mark showed me
My loose layout or sketch before I change it
Actual Explore-C file name plus page, slide or timecode; image credit where used
tiers: Core: use large pieces and access tools; record your own choice by pointing or speaking. Keep the start, later process and final work.
Extend: make tests and record your own layout choice. Keep the start, later process and final work.
Challenge: compare two ways to space marks and explain your choice. Keep the trials, later process and final work.
checks: My artwork starts fresh and is distinct from A and B.
I tried a material or tool before choosing how to use it.
My own idea and tests are kept as process evidence.
I know the final artwork must join this trail when ready.
My saved evidence has an actual file name and page, slide or timecode.
